# WIS 2323: Final project

# Communicating about Rain Forests & Their Conservation

\vspace{0.3cm}

<!-- Instead of using traditional tests to assess your understanding of the material, we will be using what [Prof. Dan Baldassarre (SUNY Oswego)](https://twitter.com/evornithology/status/1453880536880095233/photo/1) calls #NotTest assignments. -->

## **PROJECT OVERVIEW:**

Conservation organizations, museums, zoos, governments, and universities
regularly undertake marketing initiatives to promote their conservation
objectives, increase public awareness and concern for biodiversity, and
encourage their audiences to adopt sustainable practices and lifestyles.
These campaigns often rely on visual, audio, or social media to clarify
and communicate their message, but [they are unlikely to be successful
unless they have a narrow target audience, compelling campaign materials
designed specifically for this audience, and they include a call to
action](https://ssir.org/articles/entry/stop_raising_awareness_already).

**Your assignment:** to develop materials for a campaign that
communicates to UF undergraduates the importance of rain forest 
biodiversity, and concrete steps they can take to promote rain forest conservation. The Complete Assignment requires submission of the following two sections: (1) Campaign Materials designed specifically for your target audience (120 pts), and a brief reflection on the process and product (30 pts). The assignment is due 9 December 2025.

<!-- Increasing awareness about issues for which there is the first step towards mobilizing social change. We will put aside whether or not there is indeed an "information deficit"    -->

<!-- So the awareness campaigns also need to point towards specific actions people can take to actually advance rain forest conservation. https://ssir.org/articles/entry/stop_raising_awareness_already# -->

## **PART 1: Campaign Materials (120 pts)**

As a group, please select one of the following options below. Remember: _no matter which category you choose, your campaign materials *must* include a call to action and concrete steps students can take to promote rain forest conservation_. You may find it useful to use the COMPASS Message Box to plan how best to communicate your message (see the Appendix). 


### **OPTION 1 - Social Media Content** 

A [recent survey](https://www.ap.org/ap-in-the-news/2015/survey-young-adults-do-consume-news-in-their-own-way) found that very few university students (\< 20%) actively seek out news from traditional news sources such as CNN or the New York Times. Instead, most university students (\~60%) said they got their news by bumping into it on social media platforms. This is part of a broader trend in the US, in which [U.S. adults under 30 now trust information from social media almost as much as from national news outlets](https://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2022/10/27/u-s-adults-under-30-now-trust-information-from-social-media-almost-as-much-as-from-national-news-outlets/).

Groups choosing this option will prepare FIVE (5) videos in at least different styles (explainer, street interview, day-in-the-life, parody song, travelogue, etc.) suitable for posting to tik-tok, instagram, or Youtube. _Note that you are not required to post your videos, nor do you have to appear in them (though you may if you wish to)_. Regardless of your communication format, be sure to use photos, music, or video that are in the public domain or that have been licensed under the creative commons. ([Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/) is a great source of photos you can use for free with no attribution required). **_If your group chooses this option, please submit the following via Canvas:_**

i)  FIVE (5) videos _or_ a link to a folder on a cloud server (I can provide a folder for hosting videos of you need one). The content of the video can be any topic that we covered in class - rain forest ecology, conservation, threats, stereotypes - but must have as a central anchor the idea that tropical rain forests are part of your focal audience's daily lives (and that they may be completely unaware of these connections). Each video must also include: (a) A way to learn more about the protected area, species, or topic you are discussing, and (b) one (1) specific action someone watching your video can take to advance the conservation of tropical forests in the region.

ii) A word document with the script for each videos (or questions to be asked if interviewing) and sources for the information provided or cited.

iii) the source of any images used in the video

**_Useful Information for Option 1:_** You might find this [post on TikTok trends](https://invideo.io/blog/tiktok-trends/) useful...though let's be honest, how cool can something be if there is an article telling you how cool it is? There are also free
 [templates](https://www.canva.com/create/tiktok-videos/) you can use to help you prepare your videos and a blog from the Britishj Ecological Society on how to use tik-tok to [communicate science](https://www.britishecologicalsociety.org/tiktok-tips-for-ecologists/). There is also formal research on climate-change related content in tik-tok videos [link](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8451740/) and video-based [science communications practices](https://jcom.sissa.it/article/pubid/JCOM_2403_2025_V01/) that may also be useful.

### **OPTION 2: Poster Collection**

A visually captivating poster can be a great way to communicate information and spur action; moreover, it has been argued that they are a “medium for social change” (Elizabeth Resnick) and “the scene of changing ideas and aesthetics, of cultural, social and political events” (Pierre Bernard). **_If your group chooses this option, please submit the following via Canvas:_** 

i)  THREE (3) posters sized for printing on 11×17 paper (i.e., “tabloid” or “ledger” paper) as high-quality PDF files. The posters can be either horizontal or vertical orientation. 

ii) The original files used to make the posters in MS Powerpoint, Adobe Illustrator, etc.

iv) a word document or text providing:

> (a) the information in item iv below, and
> (b) the source of any images used in the poster

iv) Each poster collection must depict either (A) protected areas in the tropics or (B) tropical plant or animal species and include the following as either visual elements *or* as text:

**_Useful Information for Option 2:_** This assignment was inspired by the iconic travel and national park posters [commissioned in thee 1930s by the WPA](https://vintagraph.com/pages/what-are-wpa-posters) as part of the New Deal (you can see the originals, which are in the public domain, [here](https://www.loc.gov/free-to-use/travel-posters/) and [here](https://www.asgardpress.com/national-park-posters-gallery/) as well as some artists' reinterpretations of them [here](https://national-park-posters.com/collections/collections), [here](https://www.rangerdoug.com/posters/), and  [here](https://vintagraph.com/collections/wpa-posters?srsltid=AfmBOopkp4AlY8elD49LVFy8BRBPKcFwligBE-FUufTsw2YzAjSIwa68)) as well as the outstanding animal posters by [OBDK](https://obdk.com/collections/posters?srsltid=AfmBOooVlBfMrsU_T5vQuXt6h_c450RvLNxZQaekX7BZjnhurF31Jij9), [Wandering Walden](https://www.etsy.com/il-en/listing/1272806873/koala-poster-animal-infographic), the AZA [SAFE Program](https://blog.graphis.com/poster-fallanofaulknerandassociates-safeprogram/), the [USFWS posters](https://www.fws.gov/library/collections/esa-50-commemorative-posters), the WWF's [anti-poaching campaign posters](https://www.nytimes.com/2013/02/20/business/media/world-wildlife-fund-anti-poaching-campaign-avoids-violent-images.html), and the NYBG's [botanical and mycological flash cards](https://www.nybgshop.org/products/nybg-mushroom-identification-flashcards-100-common-mushrooms-of-north-america?pr_prod_strat=e5_desc&pr_rec_id=f53950fda&pr_rec_pid=7658918969423&pr_ref_pid=7687087652943&pr_seq=uniform).


That said, you don't have to do your posters in any of these style - you can do anything you want: more contemporary graphic design a-la [Charley Harper](https://www.nps.gov/subjects/hfc/charley-harper-posters.htm), dramatic photo-based posters inspired by [Ansel Adams'](https://www.anseladams.com/collections/yosemite-special-edition-photographs) photographs of Yosemite or Sebastão Salgado's [Amazônia Project](https://www.bandwmag.com/articles/sebastiao-salgado-the-amazonia-project), or maybe a [collage](https://www.artmajeur.com/sennikova1202/en/artworks/14791130/surreal-landscape) or [carved woodblock](https://jeffhansondesign.com/tourism-posters) poster. 

You may also find inspiration in these [vintage tourism posters](https://duendebymadamzozo.com/vintage-travel-poster/) or the futuristic tourism posters made by NASA's [JPL](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/galleries/visions-of-the-future/).Personally, [I really love these from Swellscenes](https://swellscenes.com/). Finally, you can find lots of inspiration on Pinterest and elsewhere by search with keywords like "[Conservation Campaigns](https://za.pinterest.com/jax1703/conservation-campaigns/)", [Conservation Infographics](https://uk.pinterest.com/ConservationACE/wildlife-conservation-infographics/), or "Conservation Posters" ([Board 1](https://za.pinterest.com/shayecornish2005/conservation-posters/), [Board 2](https://in.pinterest.com/pin/424253227393754609/)). You can also see what artists are selling on platforms like [Etsy](https://www.etsy.com/search?q=wildlife+posters&ref=search_bar) and [RedBubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/animal+conservation+posters).

***The only restriction is that you can't use generative AI to generate the posters or any of the images you include in them.*** You *can* use PowerPoint, Photoshop, Illustrator, etc. to manipulate your own drawings, photographs, or graphics or to manipulate the public-domain stock photos or icons provided inside MS Powerpoint or on websites like [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/) or the Smithsonian's massive [Open Access Archive](https://www.si.edu/openaccess). You can also use photos from [flickr's Commons](https://www.flickr.com/explore/) if they are public domain or creative commons (except any labeled "no-derivatives" (i.e., CC BY-NC-ND 4.0), which don't allow manipulation of the images). If you did want to do a WPA-style poster, there are lots of websites and tutorials available for making WPA-style posters in Adobe Illustrator (e.g., [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3iwpGx_8m9c)) or Photoshop (e.g., [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5IkRKZy_EA8%20and%20%5Bhere%5D(https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uyP_A_f8deY)%20or%20%5Bhere%5D(https://centsationalstyle.com/2021/08/diy-travel-posters/)). You are welcome to use these if that's the style of poster you want to make. There are also lots of templates available online, like [these](https://playground.com/design/c/poster/national-parks), [these](https://venngage.com/templates/posters/travel), or [these](https://www.freepik.com/vectors/nature-travel-poster). However, these templates tend to be very generic and, frankly, boring. Remember that your poster must be relevant to UF students. _I'd rather see something less polished but relevant poster than a generic one that doesn't engage or is irrelevant to your focal audience._

**_Remember:_** You are not being judged on the 'quality' of the art, but on the creativity and effort.


### **OPTION 3: Propose your own Communication Materials** 

Don't like either of the options above? No problem! Propose a different way to creatively communicate about rain forests and their conservation to your fellow UF students. Below are some possibilities I came up with after a morning consuming far too much RFA-certified coffee and chocolate; you're welcome to tackle one of them or propose something else. ***If your group wants to propose a project, you need to discuss it with me first so we can define the expectations and a grading rubric.***  

- **Make a [Supercut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supercut)** of rain forest stereotypes in movies (see this for [inspiration](https://slate.com/technology/2012/11/how-to-make-a-supercut-secrets-of-the-youtube-collage-form-revealed.html) and [this tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CmXKxWmzejs))
- **Music:** Write songs about your topic and record yourselves (or a friend) performing them. Or maybe rewrite the lyrics of [these cheesy 1980's love songs](https://www.yourtango.com/2019320830/35-best-cheesy-love-songs-80s-and-90s-lyrics-so-bad-theyre-good) to be about rain forests and record those. Perform a concert for friends of the pieces you composed.
- **Art:** create artwork (any medium: digital, ceramics, painting, woodcuts, comics, stickers)
- **Data Visualizations:** Generate some data visualizations related to rain forest ecology or conservation (here some [great visualizations](https://informationisbeautiful.net/)). Or present the data in a [Dashboard](https://quarto.org/docs/gallery/#dashboards); they are relatively easy to program in [R or Python with Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/dashboards/#examples) and I can help if you get stuck.
- **Podcast:** What you do is up to you. For example, you could record the first episode of a podcast series in which you
        interview rain forest plants or animals (inspired by [*Everything is     Alive*](https://www.radiotopia.fm/podcasts/everything-is-alive)). Or maybe it's a true-crime podcast. Or movie reviews. Whatever
        you want.
- **Buzzfeed-style lists:** Compile a list of Rain Forest Fails in Advertising, Marketing, or Popular Culture (with explanations of why they are incorrect).
-  **Create or Edit Wikipedia entries** (there are lists of [requested articles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Requested_articles/Natural_sciences/Biology) and [biographies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Requested_articles/Natural_sciences#Scientists_and_people_in_science), but you can propose your own articles).
- **ENROADS Event:** organize an EN-ROADS climate simulator negotiation like the one we did in class for your roommates, sorority, fraternity, club, or team. Or maybe a Bad Jungle movie Night?
- **Stream:** Do you game? Maybe stream you playing video games about rain forests where you critique the way they present the material: [try the free demo of *Empires of the Undergrowth*](https://store.steampowered.com/app/463530/Empires_of_the_Undergrowth/), If you want to play [*Green Hell*](https://store.steampowered.com/app/815370/Green_Hell/), the game designers gave me code for a free download).
-  **Create Amazon product pages** for things they use every day that are driving deforestation (you can find the template [here](https://ditchthattextbook.com/social-media-templates/)
- **Make a course summart with the [Netflix Series template](https://ditchthattextbook.com/social-media-templates/)**. Or imagine a documentary series about a UF student on a quest to learn about rain forests. Maybe the documentary follows them as they learn about how prevalent rain forests are in their daily life, about the diversity of rain forests (e.g., ecological, cultural), about the vital role of rain forests in the global climate cycle, and about the myriad threats to rain forests. Describe the documentary and each episode using this Netflix Series Template. Be sure to think about the final episodes - does the student give up and accept dystopian future without jungles, or do they decide to take bold individual and collective action to advance rain forest conservation? Or maybe a series about a dystopia future *without* rainforests...(you can see some examples of how others have used these templates [here](http://edtechpicks.org/2019/11/netflix-template/))
- **Anything else:** No idea is too weird.

1.  What you learned from this project about the challenge of
    communicating about tropical rain forests to audiences that may not
    know much about them;
2.  Any new skills, knowledge, or information you gained this semester
    (both things we covered in class and any you learned through your
    own activities and experiences);
3.  What actions you might take going forward that will advance rain
    forest conservation

## Appendix: **The COMPASS Message Box**

There are many ways to effectively organize the scientific information
we want to communicate to non-scientists. One of these is the 'Message
Box' (Figure 1), which was developed by the organization
[COMPASS](https://www.compassscicomm.org/) to help sort and distill
information about a topic in a way that resonates *with your target
audience*. The Message Box is often used by scientists talking about
their own research when communicating with decision makers; you can use it to 
map out how to communicate about complex issues related to rain forests and 
their conservation to your target audience. The [Message Box Workbook](https://www.compassscicomm.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/The-Message-Box-Workbook.pdf) includes blank templates you can use to construct your message box prior to working on your specific project.

<center>

![The COMPASS Message Box.](.//resources/message_box.png){width="70%"}

</center>

Fill out the 5 sections to craft your message; note that the Sections 1-3 are already addressed by the assignment prompt

- ***Audience:*** Undergraduate students at UF
- ***Issue:*** Identify and describe the overarching issue or
        topic that you are addressing. This should be in very broad
        terms - the big picture - and formulated as a short, concise,
        and clear phrase. For this assignment it is "Conserving Tropical
        Rain Forests"\*\*
- ***Problems?*** What are the specific topic(s) or conservation
        issue(s) that you are addressing? This can be 1-3 more detailed
        statments. For example, for this assignment the Problem(s) could
        be "1. College students are often unaware of how important rain
        forests are to their daily lives", and "2. College students have
        limited knowledge of immediate or simple actions they can take
        to promote rain forest conservation"
- ***So What?*** Why should your audience care about the issue?
        (2-4 reasons)
- ***Solutions?*** Outline the options for solving the problem or
        addressing the consequences of the issue you are discussing. Can
        your audience do anything to help? Remind yourself of why you
        are communicating this issue/problem to this audience.
- ***Benefits?*** What good things will result from implementing
        the solution(s)? While it is important to address 'Global'
        benefits, *be sure to emphasize the local and direct benefits to
        your specific audience in ways that will resonate to them.*
